stem: A patient receives stable Schedule III buprenorphine therapy. The pharmacy proposes to combine each dose in a multi-drug single-dose pouch with the patient's other morning medications. May maintenance status justify that placement?

choices.text: Yes, because a stable maintenance regimen overrides the controlled-substance packaging restriction.
No; Schedule III drugs may not enter a multi-drug single-dose package under 247 CMR 9.08(3)(b).
No, because every controlled substance is prohibited from every form of compliance packaging.
Yes, if the patient signs a written consent to combine the medications.
Yes, if the pharmacy limits the package to a 60-day supply.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.08(3)(b) prohibits Schedule II and III controlled substances in a multi-drug-single-dose package. Buprenorphine's Schedule III status decides this proposal; maintenance status, consent and a 60-day limit do not create an exception. The rule should not be generalized into a ban on all controlled substances or every compliance-packaging format.

choice_analysis.A: Maintenance status does not override the express Schedule III prohibition.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: Schedule III may not be dispensed in the proposed multi-drug-single-dose pouch.
choice_analysis.C: This overstates both the schedules and packaging types covered by the cited clause.
choice_analysis.D: Patient consent cannot waive the regulatory prohibition.
choice_analysis.E: A duration limit does not create an exception for Schedule III.

related_facts: The prohibition is specific to Schedule II/III drugs and multi-drug-single-dose packaging.
explanation.mpje_trap: Importing the policy's 60-day concept into a separate categorical controlled-substance prohibition.

reasoning_steps: Identify the proposal as multi-drug-single-dose packaging
Reject conditions that do not create an exception to paragraph (3)(b)
